name: Sunmaxxing

lead: Sunmaxxing is the practice of building a tan to look healthier. Tanned skin was historically associated with outdoor labor, but became fashionable in the 1920s, with Coco Chanel's tan on the Riviera credited with helping [1].
UV exposure darkens skin in two ways: UVA oxidizes existing melanin quickly, and UVB damages DNA and prompts melanin production, giving a tan after two or three days that lasts weeks [1].

paras: People spend time in sunlight, use tanning oil, or use sunless options such as DHA self-tanners, bronzers and spray tans [1].

Excess UV causes sunburn, raises skin cancer risk, accelerates skin aging and can impair immunity; frequent tanning-bed use was linked to roughly triple the melanoma risk in a 2010 study [1]. The WHO, American Cancer Society and US Surgeon General have issued warnings [1].

chain: Skin darkens via melanin or DHA reaction
angle.text: A tan darkens skin tone, which people use for a healthier-looking complexion. Sunless products give a similar color without UV.

lead: Sunmaxxing refers to using sun exposure to get a tan as an appearance upgrade. Tanning's cultural meaning shifted in the 1920s from a mark of outdoor labor to a fashionable look [1].

A tan arises through UVA and UVB effects on melanin; a UVB-driven tan offers modest protection, roughly SPF 3 [1]. Health bodies warn that UV exposure raises skin cancer risk and causes photoaging [1]. Sunless methods such as DHA tanners are alternatives [1].

paras: UVA oxidizes existing melanin, causing quick, short-lived darkening; UVB damages DNA and triggers melanin production, with a tan appearing in two or three days [1].

Excess UV causes sunburn and photoaging and raises skin cancer risk, while moderate sun exposure supports vitamin D production [1]. Dark skin gives some protection but not complete protection against photoaging or melanoma [1].

timeline.event: Tanning becomes fashionable; Chanel's tan credited [1]
